name: _test_autograd_multiple_dispatch_view
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::_test_autograd_multiple_dispatch_view(Tensor(a) self) -> Tensor(a). This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full overload, keyword, return, error, aliasing and mutation contract, and no test may be removed or adapted to fit this one signature. Registered schemas supplied for this operator (verbatim): aten::_test_autograd_multiple_dispatch_view(Tensor(a) self) -> Tensor(a). Semantics derived from the tests: a test-only CompositeExplicitAutograd op whose body is self.view(-1), so it is a metadata-only flat view that allocates no device payload and performs no computation. The single returned Tensor aliases the input storage: dtype, device, shape, stride, storage_offset, data_ptr and untyped_storage data_ptr match the native flat view, and the result is a view that preserves the input's lazy conjugate and negative bits. The call raises RuntimeError when the layout admits no flat view (transposed, permuted, or odd-stepped non-contiguous inputs). Because the result aliases the input, in-place writes through the returned tensor mutate the original base tensor storage. Autograd is supported and device-dispatched: the native autograd entry is device-registered, and the CUDA backward registration adds 1 to the incoming gradient, while the forward stays value-preserving. A pure definition represents only the representative overload; layout, aliasing, mutation, backward and error behavior for the other registered semantics remain owned by the original pytest.
